C-PAIR-AUDIT-MINT-CWD-1-ED6B7D22.Summary: Two staged findings — `F250` and `F251` — are in the record's hold-out buffer and not in the record, and both name this bundle's surfaces. **`F250`:** `ngrace review --change`'s attempt-pair audit pairs each task's *last* fail with the next pass, so a task recording two honest red-first pairs as fail, fail, pass, pass has one fail never audited and one pass never paired — driven at this commit against a fixture bundle, `fail, fail, pass, pass` audits **1** pair (should be 2), a pass-only task audits 0 pairs and raises nothing (the `F9.7` blind spot), and `fail, pass, fail` audits 1 pair and says nothing about the trailing red. The fix pairs on order, not on a single last-fail slot: every fail is queued per task and the next pass for that task consumes the oldest queued fail, so two consecutive reds are two audited pairs; an attempt the pairing cannot pair becomes one of two new `review.*` findings — an unpaired **fail** (a red never resolved) is `warning`, `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-fail`, and an unpaired **pass** (no preceding red) is `info`, `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-pass`. The split is measured: over the archive's 96 `run-ledger.xml` files, 76 hold attempt events and 73 of those (161 attempts — 106 unpaired passes, 55 unpaired fails) would fire the drafted single-warning rule, because the verification-only closing task every bundle carries records pass-only attempts; the `info` severity sits below the review's default `warning` threshold, so `F9.7`'s blind spot becomes visible on request (`--severity info`) without an ack on every close. **`F251`:** `resolveBranch` in `src/grace-generate.ts` runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` with no `cwd`, so `spec new --path <project B>` hashes the *shell's* branch. Driven at this commit from this working tree against a `--path` git repo on `branch-b`, the mint line reads `branch=c-pair-audit-mint-cwd`; the gitless-`--path` converse mints instead of refusing. The fix runs git with `cwd` = the resolved `--path` root. **The teaching:** one sentence in `ngrace-execute`'s attempt kind says a task with more than one red-first pair interleaves them so each is paired positionally, in canonical and packaged trees, pinned by a new `check-teaching-surface` needle. **The payment:** the buffer's two entries flush into `findings.xml` with two index `Entry` lines, and one live chartered row `C-PAIR-AUDIT-MINT-CWD-1-ED6B7D22` pays both; the close's `--retire` moves three. This is the first hashed mint in this repository, and this spec is its first real use of the `ngrace-spec`/`ngrace-plan` hashed-mint path changed by PR #97.
C-PAIR-AUDIT-MINT-CWD-1-ED6B7D22.Problem: **One finding is a pairing defect; the other is a branch-source defect.** `F250` (measured 2026-09-14 at `7ef317c`, the close of `C-TEACH-DRIVE-BEFORE-APPROVE-2`) records that `ngrace review --change` reported `Attempt-pair audit: ran over 2 fail→pass pair(s)` over two tasks that together held **eight** attempts (each task: fail, fail, pass, pass). `src/review/core.ts:1466-1488` builds pairs with `lastFailByTask`, a single `Map<task, event>`: a fail overwrites the task's previous fail, the next pass pairs with that one and deletes it, and a pass with no pending fail is skipped. So a task with two red-first pairs has its **first** fail never audited and its second pass never paired; the `review.attempt-pair-identical-tree` guard (`C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY`) covers half of a two-pair task, and a fabricated first pair passes the audit unread. Re-driven at this commit against a hand-built run/ fixture: `fail, fail, pass, pass` → `pairCount=1`; a pass-only task → `pairCount=0` and zero findings; `fail, pass, fail` → `pairCount=1` and zero findings (the trailing fail is dropped). `F9.7` already recorded the pass-only half as a blind spot — *"No fail, no pair, no finding … Recording only a pass does not defeat the check; it never engages it"* — and `F250` is its remedy. **The remedy's shape was ruled (V-B).** An unpaired *fail* is a `warning`; an unpaired *pass* is `info`, below the default `warning` threshold, because the archive measurement shows the pass half is dominated by a structural, legitimate cause — the verification-only closing task. Two codes are required because one severity per code is enforced (`makeFinding` reads `guide?.severity ?? "error"`), so the drafted single code cannot carry both severities. An unpaired pass is visible on request (`--severity info`), not on every close. **`F251`** (measured 2026-09-14 at `f5d1362`, the close of `C-HASHED-BUNDLE-IDS-2`) records that `resolveBranch` (`src/grace-generate.ts:148`) falls through `--branch` and `NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH` to `execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"])` with no `cwd` option, so git answers for the *process's* working directory while `--path` names the project the mint writes into. Driven at this commit, both directions: from this working tree (`c-pair-audit-mint-cwd`) with `NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH` unset and `--path` a git repo on `branch-b`, the mint line reads `branch=c-pair-audit-mint-cwd` and hashes that name; from the same git working tree with a gitless `--path`, `spec new` exits 0 and mints with the cwd's branch instead of refusing. `C-HASHED-BUNDLE-IDS-2`'s Constraint names `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` without saying *where* it runs, which is why nothing caught it: every drive that session ran from the project root, where the two coincide. **Both findings are in the hold-out buffer, not the record.** `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` holds exactly two entries as of 2026-09-14 — findings `f250` and `f251` (measured by the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown`: two entries, `chartered` 0, `registryHeadingIndex` -1, anchors adjacent to their `###` headings). The findings live root reads `base="7522" headroom="311" ceiling="7833"` with **207** live `<Finding>` children; the two rendered elements measure **22** and **17** lines (39 total), inside the window. The two bodies cite no internal fragment, so the wave has no citation dependency and may land in buffer order. **No decision is chartered here.** A search of the live rulings for `attempt`, `pair`, `cwd` and `branch` (61 live decisions) finds no decision that codifies the attempt-pair pairing rule or the spec mint's branch source; the only rulings hit are incidental prose (`D8.4`'s calibration pairs, `D25`'s unmerged branch, `D1.3`'s "a new review finding"). `D38` (the `C-<SLUG>-<N>-<HASH>` builder) is already paid and retired; a `cwd` fix does not reopen it because `D38` decides the *hash inputs*, and this bundle does not change them — it changes which repository the branch input is read from.

Goals.Goal: **`F250` product half — pair on order, and account for every attempt.** Replace `lastFailByTask` in `loadAttemptPairsFromBundle` (`src/review/core.ts`) with a per-task FIFO queue of unpaired fails: iterate the change's folded-ledger and loose attempt events sorted by id (the existing merge), and for each event, on `fail` push it onto that task's queue; on `pass`, if the queue is non-empty shift its oldest entry and emit the pair (fail id, pass id, fail digests, pass digests), else emit an **unpaired-pass finding**; after the loop, every fail still queued emits an **unpaired-fail finding**. The rule is positional because the payload is positional: `readAttemptPayload` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:2206`) returns a `FailureSignature` **only on fail events** (`recordAttempt` throws when a fail has no signature and never attaches one to a pass), so a pair cannot be keyed by the *pass's* signature — *"every fail in order with the next pass for that task"* is the only rule the recorded data can implement. The existing identical-tree comparison (`auditAttemptPairWriteEvidence`) runs unchanged over the pairs the new rule produces. The audit line `Attempt-pair audit: ran over N fail→pass pair(s) …` keeps its form; `N` is now the true pair count, and unpaired attempts surface as findings, not as a suppressed count.

**`F250` second half — two review findings, one per unpaired shape.** Add two exported constants and two `REVIEW_CATALOG` guides in `src/review/catalog.ts` — the same file and the same constant-plus-catalog-entry shape `ATTEMPT_PAIR_FINDING_CODE` uses (the precedent's registration site): `ATTEMPT_PAIR_UNPAIRED_FAIL_FINDING_CODE = "review.attempt-pair-unpaired-fail"` at severity `warning` (a red never resolved), and `ATTEMPT_PAIR_UNPAIRED_PASS_FINDING_CODE = "review.attempt-pair-unpaired-pass"` at severity `info` (a green with no preceding red). One severity per code is forced by the engine: a finding's severity comes from its catalog guide, `makeFinding` (`src/review/core.ts:367` at this commit) reads `guide?.severity ?? "error"`, and no per-finding severity override exists. Two codes, not one, because the two shapes carry different costs: an unpaired **fail** is an unresolved red and deserves the same `warning` as `review.attempt-pair-identical-tree` ("detection requiring adjudication"); an unpaired **pass** was measured as an artifact of the verification-only closing task and is `info`, the first `info` code in `REVIEW_CATALOG`, so it sits below the default `warning` threshold and appears only on request. Both findings carry the stable anchor `attempt-pair:unpaired:<task>:<eventId>` (one per unpaired attempt); each message names the task, the event id and its outcome and states its half — *red-first not corroborated* or *the red was never resolved*. Registering two codes forces the four catalog-completeness/cardinality instruments plus the severity-vocabulary pin, named in the Constraints.

**The pairing rule, pinned — and what it is not.** `loadAttemptPairsFromBundle` (`src/review/core.ts`) keeps its input (folded ledger events plus loose `run/` events, merged and sorted by id), its `kind === "attempt"` filter, its `readAttemptPayload` read, and its `contentDigestsFromEvidence` extraction; only the pairing state changes from one last-fail slot per task to a FIFO queue per task, and the unpaired attempts emit the new finding. **The two unpaired shapes, pinned, and their severities.** The audit raises `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-pass` (`info`) for a **pass with no queued fail** for its task — `F9.7`'s pass-only blind spot — and `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-fail` (`warning`) for a **fail with no following pass** for its task, after all events are consumed. The audit raises **no** finding for a task with no attempts at all (the `F9.6` table's "no attempts" row), and raises **no** unpaired finding for the `fail, fail, pass, pass` fixture (both fails consume a pass). A trailing fail is a finding here, not "already covered": the cursor state after an attempt is `in-progress` whether the attempt passed or failed (`src/grace-cursor.ts:330-334` at this commit), so the ledger surfaces no "task left red" fact on any other review output, and the audit is where an attempt that its rule cannot pair belongs. **Why the pass half is `info` and not `warning`:** measured over the archive's 96 `run-ledger.xml` files, 76 hold attempt events and 73 of those (161 unpaired attempts — 106 passes, 55 fails) would fire the drafted single-warning rule, and the cause is structural — the verification-only closing task every bundle carries records pass-only attempts because a suite drive has nothing to fail first (driven: `C-TEACH-DRIVE-BEFORE-APPROVE-2` `T-003` events 20 and 31 are unpaired passes; `C-HASHED-BUNDLE-IDS-2` `T-006` event 35). AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PAIR-PAIRING:
A task whose recorded attempts are, in id order, fail, fail, pass, pass yields exactly two audited fail→pass pairs — pair 1 the first fail with the first pass, pair 2 the second fail with the second pass — and no unpaired finding (neither `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-fail` nor `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-pass`); the review's `attemptPairAudit.pairCount` is 2 and the identical-tree rule runs over both pairs. A single fail→pass pair still yields one pair, and a task with no attempts yields none. The instrument is a production assertion the plan adds to `src/review/core.test.ts` (a fixture bundle whose `run/` holds the four attempt events, driven through the public review surface, or a newly exported pure pairing helper). Red direction, driven at this commit on a throwaway copy: before the fix the same four-attempt fixture reports `pairCount=1`. This criterion is invariant under the close: the close's ceremony edits no `src/` file.
bun test --timeout=30000 src/review/core.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-UNPAIRED-FINDING:
Two codes are declared once each as exported constants and registered in `REVIEW_CATALOG` with `family: "process-audit"`: `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-fail` (`ATTEMPT_PAIR_UNPAIRED_FAIL_FINDING_CODE`, severity `warning`) and `review.attempt-pair-unpaired-pass` (`ATTEMPT_PAIR_UNPAIRED_PASS_FINDING_CODE`, severity `info`). The audit raises the pass code for a pass with no queued fail for its task (a pass-only task raises one finding; a `fail, pass, pass` task raises one for the second pass) and the fail code for a trailing fail with no following pass (a `fail, pass, fail` task raises one for the third event). The `fail, fail, pass, pass` fixture raises neither, and a task with no attempts raises neither. Each finding carries a stable `findingId` and the anchor `attempt-pair:unpaired:<task>:<eventId>`. The `info` severity is below the review's default `warning` threshold, so an unpaired pass is absent from a default report and present under `--severity info`, while an unpaired fail appears by default. The instruments are the production assertions the plan adds to `src/review/core.test.ts`. Red direction, driven at this commit on a throwaway copy: the same fixtures raise nothing today. This criterion is invariant under the close.
bun test --timeout=30000 src/review/core.test.ts
